title: Dimension lower bound for a polynomial quotient over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $m\ge t\ge0$ integers, and $f_1,\dots,f_t\in k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. If $T=k[x_1,\dots,x_m]/(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ is nonzero, then the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is at least $m-t$.

source.place: Algebra, paragraph following Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), applying Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space) and Tag 00KW (lemma-one-equation) at a maximal ideal containing the equations; same lower bound implicit in Tag 00ST

proof.text: Put $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$, $J=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ and let $\pi:P\to T=P/J$ be the quotient map. Since $T\neq0$, the zero ideal of $T$ is proper, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] gives a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\subset T$. Its inverse image $\mathfrak M=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$ is a maximal ideal of $P$: indeed $P/\mathfrak M\cong T/\mathfrak n$ is a field. Moreover $J\subseteq\mathfrak M$, and the correspondence of ideals for the quotient identifies $\mathfrak n$ with $\mathfrak M/J$.

source.place: Algebra, paragraph following Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), lines 35834-35849: choose a maximal ideal containing the equations; existence also follows from Lemma Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), item (2)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension], $\dim(P_{\mathfrak M})=m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], this is $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak M)$, while $\dim(T_{\mathfrak n})=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak n)$. The Noetherian ring $P$ is the finite type algebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ over the Noetherian field $k$, hence is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] to $J=(f_1,\dots,f_t)\subseteq\mathfrak M$ gives $m=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak M)\leq\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak M/J)+t=\dim(T_{\mathfrak n})+t$. Therefore $\dim(T_{\mathfrak n})\geq m-t$. This is exactly the source's iteration of Tag 00KW at the maximal ideal $\mathfrak M$.

source.place: Algebra, paragraph following Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), lines 35834-35849, using Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space) and Tag 00KW (lemma-one-equation) t times

proof.text: The ring $T$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, being the quotient of $P$ by $J$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring], applied to the maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, identifies the dimension at $\mathfrak n$ of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ with $\dim(T_{\mathfrak n})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions], the Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ is the supremum of its dimensions at points, so it is at least its dimension at $\mathfrak n$. Step 2 therefore gives $\dim(\operatorname{Spec}T)\geq\dim(T_{\mathfrak n})\geq m-t$, as required.
